issues.legal_issue: The death sentence is appropriate for murders involving extreme brutality and grave criminality that fall within the rarest of rare cases.
material_facts: Two appellants were convicted of murdering two young women in a coordinated, cold-blooded attack and received death sentences.
The victims were attacked with sharp weapons; one victim’s neck was severed, and the other was fatally wounded after her hand was chopped off.
The court found that the murders were committed out of greed and personal vengeance arising from a property dispute.
The appeal was argued mainly on the question of sentence, and the court found no reason to interfere with the death sentences.
issues.conclusion: The murders fell within the rarest of rare cases, and the death sentences were confirmed as appropriate punishment and as a measure of social necessity and deterrence.
issues.legal_principle: Punishment must fit the crime, and courts must impose proper punishment according to the degree of criminality and the desirability of that punishment. Under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, death may be imposed in cases meeting the rarest-of-rare test described in Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab and elaborated in Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab. The court considered extreme brutality and the need for social protection and deterrence.

rule.if: capital_sentence_appeal and multiple_victims_killed and extreme_brutality and personal_vengeance_motive

predicates.capital_sentence_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which the appropriateness of a death sentence is considered.
predicates.multiple_victims_killed: The offenders killed more than one victim.
predicates.extreme_brutality: The killings were carried out with extreme brutality.
predicates.personal_vengeance_motive: The offenders committed the killings to exact personal vengeance.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a death sentence and the offenders killed multiple victims with extreme brutality to exact personal vengeance, the death sentence is confirmed.
